name: Funkhaus
classification_notes: Developed for a live-music poster series and used at bold, noisy scale, this sits as a display face rather than a text typeface.
summary: A bold poster display face grown out of Nguyen Gobber's noisy, music-driven visual work.
description: Funkhaus is one of Nguyen Gobber's 2026 typeface releases, built out of the studio's poster series for live music that turns performances into noisy visuals. It reads as a display face suited to high-impact, large-scale use rather than running text. One of the newer, less thoroughly documented entries in the studio's small catalogue.
foundry_blurb: Nguyen Gobber's practice evolved into a fully-fledged independent type foundry with the 2026 release of Sticks, Funkhaus and Type Tinker.

name: Sticks
classification_notes: Built as a type-design exercise from a 1960s modular design challenge, constructed step-by-step from geometric primitives, so it reads as a modular geometric display face.
summary: A modular display face built from a 1960s type-design exercise, constructed from repeated geometric primitives.
description: Sticks takes a design challenge from the 1960s and reworks it into a full typeface, built letter by letter from circles and simple strokes rather than drawn freehand. The process is deliberately visible in the finished forms. A research-driven, experimental release rather than a general-purpose family.
foundry_blurb: Nguyen Gobber describes Sticks as part of their 2026 foundry launch, alongside Funkhaus and the digital typographic playground Type Tinker.

name: Farmacia
classification_notes: A condensed grotesque built from the oddities of found pharmacy signage, with formal quirks in individual letters rather than a systematic design.
summary: A condensed headline grotesque with quirks lifted from a Basel pharmacy sign.
description: Farmacia reinterprets MT Grotesque Condensed through the lens of found signage on a Basel pharmacy, keeping the oddities: a bent-postured C, an upward-diagonal K, and sharp spikes on the M and W. Circular alternates for C, G, O and Q add rhythm at large sizes. Built for headlines and wordmarks, not text.
foundry_blurb: Nguyen Gobber describe Farmacia as an interpretation of MT Grotesque Condensed optimised for big headlines, gaining its character from formal peculiarities seen in the signage for a pharmacy in Basel.

name: Farmacia Soft
classification_notes: A rounded extension of Farmacia's condensed grotesque, with every sharp corner softened and optically corrected.
summary: The rounded, warmer sibling of Farmacia, with every sharp corner softened.
description: Farmacia Soft takes the parent family's condensed grotesque and rounds off its sharp corners, following up with optical corrections to keep it feeling deliberate rather than just smoothed over. Circular alternates for C, G, O and Q carry over from Farmacia. A gentler option where the original feels too blunt.
foundry_blurb: Nguyen Gobber describe Farmacia Soft as based on Farmacia, with all sharp corners rounded and optically corrected for a gentler, noticeably warmer appearance, extended in 2025.

name: Lucifer
classification_notes: Deliberately menacing letterforms drawing on early 20th-century gothic lettering place this in the display category rather than a working text style.
summary: A deliberately menacing display face drawing on the work of early 20th-century designer Robert Stöcklin.
description: Lucifer digs into the lettering of early 20th-century designer Robert Stöcklin for a display face with real bite. It's built for impact rather than legibility at small sizes. One of the studio's more overtly expressive, single-purpose releases.
foundry_blurb: Nguyen Gobber describe Lucifer as their 'menacing' typeface, delving into the work of early 20th-century designer Robert Stöcklin.

name: Hofmann
classification_notes: Built strictly on a four-by-four dot grid as a design exercise, this is a modular display face rather than a general text typeface.
summary: A modular display face built on a four-by-four dot grid, taken from an exercise in Armin Hofmann's design manual.
description: Hofmann grew out of the studio's research into the teaching materials of Basel School of Design tutors from the 1950s and 60s, specifically an exercise from Armin Hofmann's Graphic Design Manual. Every letter is built from the same four-by-four dot grid. A research piece as much as a working typeface.
foundry_blurb: Nguyen Gobber's Hofmann typeface began after Hoang Nguyen and David Gobber dug into the teachings and manuals of Basel School of Design's teachers practising in the 1950s and 60s, built around a four-by-four dot grid.

name: Kiosk
classification_notes: Simple, decisive shapes built for strong visual presence at poster scale place this as a display face.
summary: A confident poster display face built from decisive, simple shapes.
description: Kiosk is built for posters, with bold main glyphs that contrast against deliberately thinner punctuation, arrows and mathematical symbols. The result is a face with a strong, assertive presence at large sizes. Single weight, purpose-built for display use.
foundry_blurb: Nguyen Gobber describe Kiosk as an expressive display typeface intended for poster design, its dominant appearance coming from decisive, simple shapes with a strong visual presence.

name: Generation Mono
classification_notes: Despite the name, this reads as an extremely heavy, ultra-wide monoline display face rather than a fixed-width monospace, so it's classified as display.
summary: An extremely heavy, ultra-wide display face originally drawn for an annual student design campaign.
description: Generation Mono started with a handful of characters drawn for the 2019 Next Generation campaign at the Basel Academy of Art and Design, later expanded to a full basic Latin set. Its ultra-wide proportions suit vertical setting as much as horizontal. Offered on a pay-what-you-want basis.
foundry_blurb: Nguyen Gobber describe Generation Mono as an extremely heavy sans serif whose design is ultra-wide and lends itself to being set vertically, just as in its first application.

name: Monopol
classification_notes: An all-caps typeface with sharp angles and consistent strokes built for headlines and wordmarks, placing it as an expressive display face.
summary: An expressive all-caps display face with sharp geometric shapes, running from a bold standalone release to a full variable system.
description: Monopol started life as a standalone Bold in 2020, gained a Thin weight and a compact Kompakt cut the following year, then was fully reworked and expanded as Monopol 2.0 in 2024. Five predefined styles plus a variable font let it swing from an elegant lightweight to a heavy, confident headline face. Built for posters and wordmarks rather than text.
foundry_blurb: Nguyen Gobber describe Monopol as an expressive all-caps typeface with clean, geometric shapes and resolute aesthetics, ideal for strong headlines, impactful posters and striking wordmarks.
